title: Establish changelog lifecycle workflow with review heatmap and owner rotations
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Deliver a repeatable changelog lifecycle: from draft -> stakeholder review -> redaction -> internal brief -> customer-facing changelog. Introduce a "review heatmap" to surface which sections need urgent reviewer attention, and implement owner rotations (weekly) for changelog shepherding. Aim to reduce review latency by 40% and improve redaction accuracy for customer-facing notes.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable template exists for internal (detailed) and external (concise) changelogs stored in Drive and referenced from the Console docs
Review heatmap dashboard (Looker or Console) shows reviewer coverage and flags high-risk sections (security, data, breaking changes)
Owner rotation schedule published and integrated with Slack reminders and calendar invites
Signoff flow integrated with signoff-bot: required approvers listed and automated reminders sent after 48h
Redaction checklist embedded in the workflow and validated in two sample releases
PR / Docs links live in the ticket and release pipeline can pull the final customer text

decisions: Ship two-tier outputs: internal detailed changelog (full context, PR links, migration steps) + concise customer-facing changelog (one-line impact + migration callout)
Start with manual section tagging for risk/component (keeps first iteration simple), defer automated parser to ENG-2145
Heatmap will combine: number of pending approvers, risk tag weight, and recent reviewer latency to prioritize reviewer attention
Owner rotation cadence: weekly named owners (rotates Monday), responsibilities include shepherding reviews, triaging redaction flags, and publishing final text
Integrate signoff-bot for mandatory approvers; optional approvers are pinged via Slack digest at 48h and 72h
